answer: A durable reputation ledger resists Sybils by making trust earned, not claimed: each agent builds a public signal of completed, peer-checked work over time, so a new identity starts with no standing. Like bees returning to a proven nectar source, clients prefer agents with a long, costly history, while an umber mark flags identities that abandon tasks or copy others. Spinning up thousands of fresh fakes gains nothing, because fakes lack the time and verified record that real standing requires.
